learningObjective: Explain when CUDA Graphs help LLM inference and what limitation they impose on batch composition.
stem: Which characterization of CUDA Graphs in LLM inference is correct?

options.text: CUDA Graphs re-order kernels for better cache reuse across a captured region; the primary benefit is fusion of adjacent kernels into a single hardware unit that runs at higher SM utilization than the individual kernels combined.

CUDA Graphs amortize per-kernel launch overhead by capturing a sequence of kernels once and replaying it many times. For LLM decode (many small kernels per step), replay eliminates most CPU-side dispatch cost. The limitation is that the shape and memory layout must match the captured version; batch composition changes require different graphs (or falling back to eager).

CUDA Graphs are only useful for compute-bound workloads; memory-bound kernels do not benefit because their runtime is dominated by HBM traffic, not launch overhead. LLM decode is memory-bound and thus CUDA Graphs provide no wall-clock benefit.

CUDA Graphs automatically fuse kernels across their captured region into a smaller number of hardware kernels; the fusion is opaque to the user but is the source of the throughput improvement in inference workloads.

explanation: CUDA Graphs let you record a sequence of kernel launches once and replay them repeatedly with a single CPU-side submit call. This amortizes launch overhead — critical for LLM decode where each step has many small kernels (attention, GEMV, norms, sampling), often 20-50 µs each with 5-20 µs of CPU dispatch between them. The limitation is capture-replay determinism: shapes, pointers, and control flow must match the captured version. In serving, this forces per-batch-shape graphs (e.g., one per common batch size) or fallback for uncommon shapes.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: CUDA Graphs do not fuse or reorder kernels; they replay them faster.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: many small memory-bound kernels are exactly where CUDA Graphs pay off (launch gaps between them are eliminated).
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: no automatic fusion; the graph is a fixed sequence of the same kernels.

assumptions: Kernels have known static shapes at capture time.
nonImplications: Does not imply CUDA Graphs help every workload; large kernels dominated by their own compute see little benefit.
Does not imply Graphs are incompatible with continuous batching; frameworks typically capture graphs for a set of common batch sizes.

performanceClaim.scope: CUDA Graph benefit for LLM decode and its shape/layout limitation
